87# Flush-time batching limits shared by every MongoDB upsert path 

88# (MongoVectorDBStorage, MongoKVStorage, MongoGraphStorage). 

89# The payload-byte budget is the primary limiter; the record-count caps are a 

90# secondary guard that only binds when individual records are small. 

91# Upsert and delete have separate count caps on purpose: upsert records each 

92# carry a full embedding vector and are far heavier than delete _ids, so the 

93# upsert batch count is kept much smaller than the delete one. 

94# MongoDB caps a single BSON document at 16MB and a single bulk command message 

95# at 48MB; a 16MB JSON estimate (which overestimates the real BSON size) keeps 

96# every bulk_write comfortably below the wire limit and bounds peak memory. 

97DEFAULT_MONGO_UPSERT_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024 # 16MB 

98DEFAULT_MONGO_UPSERT_MAX_RECORDS_PER_BATCH = 128 

99DEFAULT_MONGO_DELETE_MAX_RECORDS_PER_BATCH = 1000 

100 

101# get_edges_batch's own $or chunk size, matching postgres_impl.get_edges_batch's 

102# batch_size default -- a fixed safety cap for query size, not an operator-tuned 

103# knob like the env-var-driven limits above, so it isn't one. 

104_GET_EDGES_BATCH_CHUNK_SIZE = 500 

105 

106# node_degrees_batch's own $in chunk size -- kept as its own constant rather 

107# than sharing _GET_EDGES_BATCH_CHUNK_SIZE since the two methods' per-entry 

108# BSON size differs enough to matter: a bare id string costs far less than 

109# get_edges_batch's two-field edge_lo/edge_hi dict, so the same query-size 

110# budget affords a much larger chunk here. Matched to 

111# _GRAPH_DEGREE_RANK_MAX_CANDIDATES (this module's already-accepted safe 

112# candidate-set size for a BFS level) rather than picked independently, so 

113# that already-bounded caller stays at 2 round trips (one chunk) instead of 

114# being re-split by an unrelated, smaller cap. 

115_NODE_DEGREES_BATCH_CHUNK_SIZE = 8192 

116 

117# Shared query payload budget for node-degree ``$in`` and edge ``$or`` lookups. 

118# Count-only caps cannot bound BSON size because entity IDs are caller-controlled. 

119# Reserve 1 MiB for query wrappers and BSON metadata; count caps remain secondary 

120# guards on round-trip volume. 

121_GRAPH_BATCH_QUERY_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 15 * 1024 * 1024 # 15 MiB + 1 MiB headroom 

122 

123# MongoDB duplicate-key error code, raised when an upsert insert races the 

124# unique edge-endpoint index (another writer inserted the same edge first). 

125_DUPLICATE_KEY_CODE = 11000 

126 

127# Emit a migration progress line every this many deduped docs, so operators 

128# watching a large migration see liveness (mirrors the OpenSearch canonical-id 

129# migration's progress cadence). 

130_EDGE_MIGRATION_PROGRESS_INTERVAL = 50_000 

131 

132# Ceiling on how many same-depth candidates get a degree lookup before the 

133# max_nodes cap in the bidirectional BFS. node_degrees_batch itself chunks 

134# its $in queries at this same size (see _NODE_DEGREES_BATCH_CHUNK_SIZE), so 

135# this call site fits in exactly one chunk -- 2 round trips, same as before 

136# chunking existed -- when ids are short enough to stay under 

137# _GRAPH_BATCH_QUERY_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES; long ids can still re-split it (see 

138# that constant's comment), the count cap alone is not a hard guarantee. The 

139# ceiling itself still earns its keep: one hub can put 100k+ neighbours in a 

140# single level, and without it every one of them would get degree-ranked (in 

141# several chunks) for an outcome max_nodes will mostly discard anyway. 

142# (Deliberately not shared with the OpenSearch constant of the same value: 

143# that one is derived from index.max_terms_count / search.max_buckets.) 

144_GRAPH_DEGREE_RANK_MAX_CANDIDATES = 8192

147def _canonical_edge_endpoints( 

148 source_node_id: str, target_node_id: str 

149) -> tuple[str, str]: 

150 """Direction-independent ``(edge_lo, edge_hi)`` endpoints for an undirected edge. 

151 

152 The sorted pair maps ``(A,B)`` and ``(B,A)`` to the same two field values, 

153 so a *compound* unique index on ``(edge_lo, edge_hi)`` lets MongoDB reject 

154 the second of two racing inserts (the classic ``$or``-upsert duplicate gap) 

155 regardless of direction. Storing the endpoints as two separate fields — not 

156 a single delimiter-joined string — avoids any collision between distinct 

157 pairs whose ids happen to contain the delimiter (e.g. custom-KG ids), and 

158 needs no input sanitisation. Reads keep using the bidirectional ``$or``. 

159 """ 

160 return tuple(sorted((source_node_id, target_node_id))) # type: ignore[return-value]

172def _coerce_weight(weight: Any) -> float | None: 

173 """Coerce a (possibly string) edge weight to float, or None if the value 

174 is missing, non-numeric, or not finite. 

175 

176 NaN/+-inf pass ``float()`` (including via strings like "nan"), but none of 

177 them is a storable graph attribute (see ``graph_attribute_value_rejection`` 

178 -- the rule is the portability intersection across the backends, not a 

179 per-backend impossibility) and a NaN poisons every ``sum``/``max`` it later 

180 reaches. A non-finite legacy weight is therefore unusable in exactly the 

181 way a non-numeric one is, and is skipped the same way. 

182 """ 

183 if weight is None: 

184 return None 

185 try: 

186 coerced = float(weight) 

187 except (TypeError, ValueError): 

188 return None 

189 return coerced if math.isfinite(coerced) else None

192def _estimate_doc_bytes(doc: Any) -> int: 

193 """Estimate a document's serialized byte size via compact JSON. 

194 

195 JSON overestimates the real BSON size MongoDB writes (a JSON float string is 

196 far longer than the 8 bytes a BSON double encodes), so callers stay 

197 conservatively below server limits and never underestimate. 

198 

199 This is a splitting *heuristic*, not the exact wire size: upsert callers pass 

200 only the dominant payload field (the ``$set`` body / ``update_doc``), not the 

201 full ``UpdateOne`` op (filter, ``$setOnInsert``, ``$or`` wrapper). Those extras 

202 are tiny next to an embedding/document body, and the 16MB estimate budget sits 

203 far under MongoDB's 48MB bulk-command limit, so the under-count is immaterial; 

204 the server stays the final arbiter. 

205 """ 

206 return len( 

207 json.dumps(doc, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"), default=str).encode( 

208 "utf-8" 

209 ) 

210 ) 

211

213def _chunk_by_budget( 

214 items: list[Any], 

215 size_of, 

216 max_payload_bytes: int, 

217 max_records_per_batch: int, 

218) -> list[tuple[list[Any], int]]: 

219 """Split items into batches by estimated payload size (primary) and count. 

220 

221 The byte budget is the primary limiter: items accumulate until adding the 

222 next one would exceed ``max_payload_bytes``, then a new batch starts. 

223 ``size_of(item)`` returns an item's estimated serialized byte size. A single 

224 item larger than the byte budget is emitted as its own batch rather than 

225 raising; the server stays the final arbiter. A non-positive limit disables 

226 that dimension. Returns ``(batch, summed_estimated_bytes)`` tuples (the 

227 estimate is used for logging). 

228 """ 

229 if not items: 229 ↛ 230line 229 didn't jump to line 230 because the condition on line 229 was never true

230 return [] 

231 

232 payload_limit = max_payload_bytes if max_payload_bytes > 0 else float("inf") 

233 records_limit = max_records_per_batch if max_records_per_batch > 0 else float("inf") 

234 

235 batches: list[tuple[list[Any], int]] = [] 

236 current: list[Any] = [] 

237 # JSON array overhead ("[]") 

238 current_bytes = 2 

239 

240 for item in items: 

241 item_bytes = size_of(item) 

242 # If current batch not empty, a comma is needed before next element. 

243 separator_overhead = 1 if current else 0 

244 next_bytes = current_bytes + separator_overhead + item_bytes 

245 

246 if current and (len(current) >= records_limit or next_bytes > payload_limit): 

247 batches.append((current, current_bytes)) 

248 current = [] 

249 current_bytes = 2 

250 next_bytes = current_bytes + item_bytes 

251 

252 current.append(item) 

253 current_bytes = next_bytes 

254 

255 if current: 255 ↛ 258line 255 didn't jump to line 258 because the condition on line 255 was always true

256 batches.append((current, current_bytes)) 

257 

258 return batches

312async def _run_batched_bulk_write( 

313 collection, 

314 ops: list[tuple[Any, int, str]], 

315 *,

337 logger.info( 

338 f"{log_prefix} {what} split into {len(batches)} batches " 

339 f"for {len(ops)} records" 

340 )

342 if ( 342 ↛ 347line 342 didn't jump to line 347 because the condition on line 342 was never true

343 len(batch) == 1

349 f"estimated {estimated_bytes} bytes exceeds {max_payload_bytes}"

351 logger.debug( 

352 f"{log_prefix} {what} batch {batch_index}/{len(batches)}: " 

353 f"records={len(batch)}, estimated_payload_bytes={estimated_bytes}" 

354 ) 

355 await collection.bulk_write([triple[0] for triple in batch], ordered=ordered)

495 async def get_by_ids(self, ids: list[str]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]: 

496 cursor = self._data.find({"_id": {"$in": ids}}) 

497 docs = await cursor.to_list(length=None) 

498 

499 doc_map: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {} 

500 for doc in docs: 

501 if not doc: 

502 continue 

503 doc.setdefault("create_time", 0) 

504 doc.setdefault("update_time", 0) 

505 doc_map[str(doc.get("_id"))] = doc 

506 

507 ordered_results: list[dict[str, Any] | None] = [] 

508 for id_value in ids:

510 return ordered_results

514 existing_ids = {str(x["_id"]) async for x in cursor} 

515 return keys - existing_ids

519 if not data:

522 # Unified handling for all namespaces with flattened keys. KV docs 

523 # (full_docs, text_chunks, llm_response_cache) can be large, so the 

524 # upsert is split into payload-bounded bulk_write batches. 

525 operations: list[tuple[Any, int, str]] = [] 

526 current_time = int(time.time()) # Get current Unix timestamp 

527 

528 for i, (k, v) in enumerate(data.items(), start=1): 

529 # For text_chunks namespace, ensure llm_cache_list field exists

532 v["llm_cache_list"] = [] 

533 

534 # Create a copy of v for $set operation, excluding create_time to avoid conflicts 

535 v_for_set = v.copy() 

536 v_for_set["_id"] = k # Use flattened key as _id 

537 v_for_set["update_time"] = current_time # Always update update_time 

538 

539 # Remove create_time from $set to avoid conflict with $setOnInsert 

540 v_for_set.pop("create_time", None)

542 operations.append( 

543 ( 

544 UpdateOne( 

545 {"_id": k}, 

546 { 

547 "$set": v_for_set, # Update all fields except create_time 

548 "$setOnInsert": { 

549 "create_time": current_time 

550 }, # Set create_time only on insert 

551 }, 

552 upsert=True, 

553 ), 

554 _estimate_doc_bytes(v_for_set), 

555 k, 

556 ) 

557 )

563 # them in parallel and is the right choice for idempotent upserts.

565 self._data, 

566 operations, 

567 max_payload_bytes=self._max_upsert_payload_bytes, 

568 max_records_per_batch=self._max_upsert_records_per_batch, 

569 ordered=False, 

570 log_prefix=f"[{self.workspace}] {self.namespace} upsert:",

651 def _prepare_doc_status_data(self, doc: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]: 

652 """Normalize and migrate a raw Mongo document to DocProcessingStatus-compatible dict.""" 

653 # Make a copy of the data to avoid modifying the original 

654 data = doc.copy() 

655 # Remove deprecated content field if it exists 

656 data.pop("content", None) 

657 # Remove MongoDB _id field if it exists 

658 data.pop("_id", None) 

659 # If file_path is not in data, use document id as file path 

660 if "file_path" not in data: 

661 data["file_path"] = "no-file-path" 

662 # Ensure new fields exist with default values 

663 if "metadata" not in data: 

664 data["metadata"] = {} 

665 if "error_msg" not in data: 

666 data["error_msg"] = None 

667 # Backward compatibility: migrate legacy 'error' field to 'error_msg' 

668 if "error" in data: 668 ↛ 669line 668 didn't jump to line 669 because the condition on line 668 was never true

669 if "error_msg" not in data or data["error_msg"] in (None, ""): 

670 data["error_msg"] = data.pop("error") 

671 else: 

672 data.pop("error", None) 

673 return data 

674 

675 def _mongo_doc_processing_status_from_doc( 

676 self, doc: dict[str, Any] 

677 ) -> DocProcessingStatus: 

678 """Normalise a raw Mongo document into a FULL DocProcessingStatus. 

679 

680 Single source of the raw -> status construction shared by 

681 ``get_docs_by_statuses`` and the ``get_full_docs_by_ids`` hydration 

682 path. Raises ``KeyError``/``TypeError`` on a malformed document 

683 (``TypeError`` is what construction raises on missing required 

684 fields); the caller decides strict (raise) vs relaxed (skip). 

685 Fields the dataclass does not declare are tolerated — see 

686 ``DocProcessingStatus.from_stored``. 

687 """ 

688 data = self._prepare_doc_status_data(doc) 

689 return DocProcessingStatus.from_stored(data)

787 async def upsert(self, data: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]) -> None: 

788 logger.debug(f"[{self.workspace}] Inserting {len(data)} to {self.namespace}") 

789 if not data: 

790 return 

791 update_tasks: list[Any] = [] 

792 for i, (k, v) in enumerate(data.items(), start=1): 

793 # Ensure chunks_list field exists and is an array 

794 if "chunks_list" not in v: 

795 v["chunks_list"] = [] 

796 data[k]["_id"] = k 

797 update_tasks.append( 

798 self._data.update_one({"_id": k}, {"$set": v}, upsert=True) 

799 ) 

800 await _cooperative_yield(i) 

801 await asyncio.gather(*update_tasks)

813 async def get_docs_by_statuses( 

814 self, statuses: list[DocStatus], strict: bool = False 

815 ) -> dict[str, DocProcessingStatus]: 

816 """Get all documents matching any of the given statuses in a single query. 

817 

818 Uses MongoDB's $in operator to fetch all matching statuses in one 

819 round-trip instead of one find() call per status. Transport errors 

820 always propagate; ``strict=True`` additionally raises on any record 

821 that cannot be converted (complete-or-raise scheduling contract, see 

822 base class). 

823 """ 

824 if not statuses: 824 ↛ 825line 824 didn't jump to line 825 because the condition on line 824 was never true

825 return {} 

826 status_values = [s.value for s in statuses] 

827 cursor = self._data.find({"status": {"$in": status_values}}) 

828 docs = await cursor.to_list(length=None) 

829 result = {} 

830 for doc in docs: 

831 try: 

832 result[doc["_id"]] = self._mongo_doc_processing_status_from_doc(doc) 

833 except (KeyError, TypeError) as e: 

834 # TypeError is what DocProcessingStatus(**data) actually raises 

835 # on missing required fields — without it here, the relaxed 

836 # skip-and-log contract silently becomes crash-the-whole-call. 

837 logger.error( 

838 f"[{self.workspace}] Missing required field for document {doc['_id']}: {e}" 

839 ) 

840 if strict: 

841 raise 

842 continue 

843 return result

846 self, track_id: str 

847 ) -> dict[str, DocProcessingStatus]: 

848 """Get all documents with a specific track_id""" 

849 cursor = self._data.find({"track_id": track_id}) 

850 result = await cursor.to_list() 

851 processed_result = {} 

852 for doc in result: 

853 doc_id_hint = doc.get("_id", "<unknown>") if doc else "<unknown>" 

854 try: 

855 processed_result[doc["_id"]] = ( 

856 self._mongo_doc_processing_status_from_doc(doc) 

857 ) 

858 except (KeyError, TypeError) as e: 

859 # TypeError, not just KeyError: DocProcessingStatus is a 

860 # dataclass, so a row missing a required field (or carrying an 

861 # unknown one) raises TypeError. Catching KeyError alone left 

862 # the real failure uncaught and crashed the whole listing. 

863 logger.error( 

864 f"[{self.workspace}] Missing required field for document " 

865 f"{doc_id_hint}: {e}" 

866 ) 

867 continue 

868 return processed_result

917 async def create_and_migrate_indexes_if_not_exists(self): 

918 """Create indexes to optimize pagination queries and migrate file_path indexes for Chinese collation""" 

919 try: 

920 # Get indexes for the current collection only 

921 indexes_cursor = await self._data.list_indexes() 

922 existing_indexes = await indexes_cursor.to_list(length=None) 

923 existing_index_names = {idx.get("name", "") for idx in existing_indexes} 

924 

925 # Define collation configuration for Chinese pinyin sorting 

926 collation_config = {"locale": "zh", "numericOrdering": True} 

927 

928 # Use workspace-specific index names to avoid cross-workspace conflicts 

929 workspace_prefix = f"{self.workspace}_" if self.workspace != "" else "" 

930 

931 # 1. Define all indexes needed with workspace-specific names 

932 all_indexes = [ 

933 # Original pagination indexes 

934 { 

935 "name": f"{workspace_prefix}status_updated_at", 

936 "keys": [("status", 1), ("updated_at", -1)], 

937 }, 

938 { 

939 "name": f"{workspace_prefix}status_created_at", 

940 "keys": [("status", 1), ("created_at", -1)], 

941 }, 

942 {"name": f"{workspace_prefix}updated_at", "keys": [("updated_at", -1)]}, 

943 {"name": f"{workspace_prefix}created_at", "keys": [("created_at", -1)]}, 

944 {"name": f"{workspace_prefix}id", "keys": [("_id", 1)]}, 

945 {"name": f"{workspace_prefix}track_id", "keys": [("track_id", 1)]}, 

946 # New file_path indexes with Chinese collation and workspace-specific names 

947 { 

948 "name": f"{workspace_prefix}file_path_zh_collation", 

949 "keys": [("file_path", 1)], 

950 "collation": collation_config, 

951 }, 

952 { 

953 "name": f"{workspace_prefix}status_file_path_zh_collation", 

954 "keys": [("status", 1), ("file_path", 1)], 

955 "collation": collation_config, 

956 }, 

957 # Partial index on content_hash for content-based dedup lookups. 

958 # Mirrors the PG partial index: skip legacy/empty values so the 

959 # index stays small and a content_hash="" query is a guaranteed miss. 

960 { 

961 "name": f"{workspace_prefix}content_hash", 

962 "keys": [("content_hash", 1)], 

963 "partialFilterExpression": { 

964 "content_hash": {"$exists": True, "$type": "string", "$gt": ""} 

965 }, 

966 }, 

967 # Keyset sweep index for the bounded scheduling page API: 

968 # matches the MUST sort of get_docs_by_statuses_page 

969 # ((created_at ASC, _id ASC) within each status branch of a 

970 # status $in — the server merges the per-status keysets). 

971 { 

972 "name": f"{workspace_prefix}status_created_at_id_asc", 

973 "keys": [("status", 1), ("created_at", 1), ("_id", 1)], 

974 }, 

975 ] 

976 

977 # 2. Handle legacy index cleanup: only drop old indexes that exist in THIS collection 

978 legacy_index_names = [ 

979 "file_path_zh_collation", 

980 "status_file_path_zh_collation", 

981 "status_updated_at", 

982 "status_created_at", 

983 "updated_at", 

984 "created_at", 

985 "id", 

986 "track_id", 

987 "content_hash", 

988 ] 

989 

990 for legacy_name in legacy_index_names: 

991 if ( 

992 legacy_name in existing_index_names 

993 and legacy_name 

994 != f"{workspace_prefix}{legacy_name.replace(workspace_prefix, '')}" 

995 ): 

996 try: 

997 await self._data.drop_index(legacy_name) 

998 logger.debug( 

999 f"[{self.workspace}] Migrated: dropped legacy index '{legacy_name}' from collection {self._collection_name}" 

1000 ) 

1001 existing_index_names.discard(legacy_name) 

1002 except PyMongoError as drop_error: 

1003 logger.warning( 

1004 f"[{self.workspace}] Failed to drop legacy index '{legacy_name}' from collection {self._collection_name}: {drop_error}" 

1005 ) 

1006 

1007 # 3. Create all needed indexes with workspace-specific names 

1008 for index_info in all_indexes: 

1009 index_name = index_info["name"] 

1010 if index_name not in existing_index_names: 

1011 create_kwargs = {"name": index_name} 

1012 if "collation" in index_info: 

1013 create_kwargs["collation"] = index_info["collation"] 

1014 if "partialFilterExpression" in index_info: 

1015 create_kwargs["partialFilterExpression"] = index_info[ 

1016 "partialFilterExpression" 

1017 ] 

1018 

1019 try: 

1020 await self._data.create_index( 

1021 index_info["keys"], **create_kwargs 

1022 ) 

1023 logger.debug( 

1024 f"[{self.workspace}] Created index '{index_name}' for collection {self._collection_name}" 

1025 ) 

1026 except PyMongoError as create_error: 

1027 # If creation still fails, log the error but continue with other indexes 

1028 logger.error( 

1029 f"[{self.workspace}] Failed to create index '{index_name}' for collection {self._collection_name}: {create_error}" 

1030 ) 

1031 else: 

1032 logger.debug( 

1033 f"[{self.workspace}] Index '{index_name}' already exists for collection {self._collection_name}" 

1034 ) 

1035 

1036 except PyMongoError as e: 

1037 logger.error( 

1038 f"[{self.workspace}] Error creating/migrating indexes for {self._collection_name}: {e}" 

1039 ) 

1040 

1041 async def get_docs_paginated( 

1042 self, 

1043 status_filter: DocStatus | None = None, 

1044 status_filters: list[DocStatus] | None = None, 

1045 page: int = 1, 

1046 page_size: int = 50, 

1047 sort_field: str = "updated_at", 

1048 sort_direction: str = "desc", 

1049 ) -> tuple[list[tuple[str, DocProcessingStatus]], int]: 

1050 """Get documents with pagination support 

1051 

1052 Args: 

1053 status_filter: Filter by document status, None for all statuses 

1054 page: Page number (1-based) 

1055 page_size: Number of documents per page (10-200) 

1056 sort_field: Field to sort by ('created_at', 'updated_at', 'id', 'file_path'). 

1057 The legacy '_id' alias is also accepted. 

1058 sort_direction: Sort direction ('asc' or 'desc') 

1059 

1060 Returns: 

1061 Tuple of (list of (doc_id, DocProcessingStatus) tuples, total_count) 

1062 """ 

1063 status_filter_values = self.resolve_status_filter_values( 

1064 status_filter=status_filter, 

1065 status_filters=status_filters, 

1066 ) 

1067 

1068 # Validate parameters 

1069 if page < 1: 1069 ↛ 1070line 1069 didn't jump to line 1070 because the condition on line 1069 was never true

1070 page = 1 

1071 if page_size < 10: 1071 ↛ 1072line 1071 didn't jump to line 1072 because the condition on line 1071 was never true

1072 page_size = 10 

1073 elif page_size > 200: 1073 ↛ 1074line 1073 didn't jump to line 1074 because the condition on line 1073 was never true

1074 page_size = 200 

1075 

1076 if sort_field == "id": 

1077 sort_field = "_id" 

1078 

1079 if sort_field not in ["created_at", "updated_at", "_id", "file_path"]: 

1080 sort_field = "updated_at" 

1081 

1082 if sort_direction.lower() not in ["asc", "desc"]: 1082 ↛ 1083line 1082 didn't jump to line 1083 because the condition on line 1082 was never true

1083 sort_direction = "desc" 

1084 

1085 # Build query filter 

1086 query_filter = {} 

1087 if status_filter_values is not None: 

1088 query_filter["status"] = {"$in": sorted(status_filter_values)} 

1089 

1090 # Get total count 

1091 total_count = await self._data.count_documents(query_filter) 

1092 

1093 # Calculate skip value 

1094 skip = (page - 1) * page_size 

1095 

1096 # Build sort criteria 

1097 sort_direction_value = 1 if sort_direction.lower() == "asc" else -1 

1098 sort_criteria = [(sort_field, sort_direction_value)] 

1099 

1100 # Query for paginated data with Chinese collation for file_path sorting 

1101 if sort_field == "file_path": 

1102 # Use Chinese collation for pinyin sorting 

1103 cursor = ( 

1104 self._data.find(query_filter) 

1105 .sort(sort_criteria) 

1106 .collation({"locale": "zh", "numericOrdering": True}) 

1107 .skip(skip) 

1108 .limit(page_size) 

1109 ) 

1110 else: 

1111 # Use default sorting for other fields 

1112 cursor = ( 

1113 self._data.find(query_filter) 

1114 .sort(sort_criteria) 

1115 .skip(skip) 

1116 .limit(page_size) 

1117 ) 

1118 result = await cursor.to_list(length=page_size) 

1119 

1120 # Convert to (doc_id, DocProcessingStatus) tuples 

1121 documents = [] 

1122 for doc in result: 

1123 try: 

1124 doc_id = doc["_id"] 

1125 

1126 data = self._prepare_doc_status_data(doc) 

1127 

1128 doc_status = DocProcessingStatus.from_stored(data) 

1129 documents.append((doc_id, doc_status)) 

1130 except KeyError as e: 

1131 logger.error( 

1132 f"[{self.workspace}] Missing required field for document {doc['_id']}: {e}" 

1133 ) 

1134 continue 

1135 

1136 return documents, total_count 

1137 

1138 async def get_all_status_counts(self) -> dict[str, int]: 

1139 """Get counts of documents in each status for all documents 

1140 

1141 Returns: 

1142 Dictionary mapping status names to counts, including 'all' field 

1143 """ 

1144 pipeline = [{"$group": {"_id": "$status", "count": {"$sum": 1}}}] 

1145 cursor = await self._data.aggregate(pipeline, allowDiskUse=True) 

1146 result = await cursor.to_list() 

1147 

1148 counts = {} 

1149 total_count = 0 

1150 for doc in result: 

1151 counts[doc["_id"]] = doc["count"] 

1152 total_count += doc["count"] 

1153 

1154 # Add 'all' field with total count 

1155 counts["all"] = total_count 

1156 

1157 return counts

1293 @staticmethod 

1294 def _encode_cursor(created_at: str | None, doc_id: str) -> str:

1297 @staticmethod 

1298 def _decode_cursor(opaque: str) -> tuple[str | None, str]:

1300 decoded = json.loads(opaque) 

1301 created, doc_id = decoded

1304 if created is not None and not isinstance(created, str): 1304 ↛ 1305line 1304 didn't jump to line 1305 because the condition on line 1304 was never true

1305 raise ValueError("cursor created_at must be a string or null") 

1306 except (ValueError, TypeError) as e:

1308 f"Malformed scheduling cursor for MongoDocStatusStorage: {e}" 

1309 ) from e

1311 

1312 @staticmethod 

1313 def _doc_cursor_key(doc: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[str | None, str]: 

1314 """(created_at, _id) keyset key of a RAW query-returned doc.

1316 A missing/null/non-string created_at encodes as ``None`` — the

1318 it as ``""`` would break the resume filter: ``{"created_at": ""}``

1324 return (created if isinstance(created, str) else None, str(doc.get("_id")))

1355 async def get_docs_by_statuses_page( 

1356 self, 

1357 statuses: list[DocStatus], 

1358 *, 

1359 limit: int, 

1360 position: CursorPosition = CURSOR_START, 

1361 strict: bool = False, 

1362 ) -> DocStatusPage: 

1363 """Bounded keyset page: one indexed ``find`` with ``sort`` + ``limit``. 

1364 

1365 ``created_at`` is stored as an ISO-8601 string, so the keyset 

1366 comparison stays string-typed end to end (cursor ↔ query ↔ sort). 

1367 

1368 Consumed-position contract: every predicate (status, keyset resume) is 

1369 evaluated SERVER-side, so the 

1370 set of query-returned docs IS the set of consumed records — the 

1371 frontier is the last RETURNED doc's ``(created_at, _id)`` key, and 

1372 fewer returned docs than ``limit`` proves the sweep is exhausted 

1373 (CURSOR_END). A relaxed-mode conversion skip drops the doc from the 

1374 page but the doc was still returned by the query, hence consumed: 

1375 the cursor advances past it (never re-read, never terminal-by-skip). 

1376 

1377 Transport/query errors always propagate (never swallowed into a 

1378 partial page); ``strict=True`` additionally raises on any returned 

1379 doc that cannot be projected to :class:`DocSchedulingRecord`. 

1380 """ 

1381 if limit <= 0: 

1382 raise ValueError(f"page limit must be positive, got {limit}") 

1383 if not statuses or position is CURSOR_END: 

1384 return DocStatusPage(docs={}, next_position=CURSOR_END) 

1385 

1386 query: dict[str, Any] = {"status": {"$in": sorted({s.value for s in statuses})}} 

1387 and_clauses: list[dict[str, Any]] = [] 

1388 if isinstance(position, CursorAfter): 

1389 created, doc_id = self._decode_cursor(position.opaque) 

1390 if created is None: 

1391 # Cursor inside the missing/null bucket (sorted first by 

1392 # BSON): continue through its remaining docs by _id — 

1393 # {"created_at": None} matches BOTH missing and null — then 

1394 # every doc with a real (non-null, existing) value. 

1395 and_clauses.append( 

1396 { 

1397 "$or": [ 

1398 {"created_at": None, "_id": {"$gt": doc_id}}, 

1399 {"created_at": {"$ne": None}}, 

1400 ] 

1401 } 

1402 ) 

1403 else: 

1404 # Past the missing/null bucket: string-typed $gt/$eq never 

1405 # match missing or null fields, which is correct — that 

1406 # bucket was already consumed before this cursor. 

1407 and_clauses.append( 

1408 { 

1409 "$or": [ 

1410 {"created_at": {"$gt": created}}, 

1411 {"created_at": created, "_id": {"$gt": doc_id}}, 

1412 ] 

1413 } 

1414 ) 

1415 if and_clauses: 

1416 query["$and"] = and_clauses 

1417 

1418 cursor = ( 

1419 self._data.find(query).sort([("created_at", 1), ("_id", 1)]).limit(limit) 

1420 ) 

1421 raw_docs = await cursor.to_list(length=limit) 

1422 

1423 docs: dict[str, DocSchedulingRecord] = {} 

1424 for doc in raw_docs: 

1425 record = self._scheduling_record_from_doc(doc, strict=strict) 

1426 if record is None: 

1427 continue # relaxed skip: query-returned, hence still consumed 

1428 docs[record.id] = record 

1429 

1430 if len(raw_docs) < limit: 

1431 return DocStatusPage(docs=docs, next_position=CURSOR_END) 

1432 last_created, last_id = self._doc_cursor_key(raw_docs[-1]) 

1433 return DocStatusPage( 

1434 docs=docs, 

1435 next_position=CursorAfter(self._encode_cursor(last_created, last_id)), 

1436 ) 

1437

1548 @staticmethod 

1549 def _conflict_fingerprint(sorted_doc_ids: list[str]) -> str:

1563 except (ValueError, TypeError) as e:

1565 f"Malformed source-conflict cursor for MongoDocStatusStorage: {e}" 

1566 ) from e

1593 { 

1594 "file_path": canonical_source_key, 

1595 "metadata.is_duplicate": {"$ne": True}, 

1596 }, 

1597 {"_id": 1},

1599 .sort([("_id", 1)]) 

1600 .limit(self._CONFLICT_SAMPLE_CAP) 

1601 )

1605 async def list_source_conflicts_page( 

1606 self, 

1607 *, 

1608 limit: int, 

1609 position: CursorPosition = CURSOR_START, 

1610 ) -> SourceConflictPage: 

1611 """Page canonical source keys with >1 primary candidate (see base). 

1612 

1613 A server-side aggregation groups PRIMARY (``metadata.is_duplicate != 

1614 true``) rows by ``file_path``, keeps groups with candidate count ≥ 2, 

1615 resumes strictly after the cursor's canonical key (``$gt``) and sorts 

1616 by canonical key so the keyset is stable. 

1617 

1618 The accumulator is COUNT-ONLY: ``$push``-ing the ids would build one 

1619 array per distinct ``file_path`` in the workspace — every group, not 

1620 just the conflicting ones, since ``candidate_count >= 2`` can only be 

1621 applied AFTER ``$group`` — so peak aggregation memory would scale with 

1622 the document count instead of the number of source keys. Samples are 

1623 instead fetched per SURFACED key (at most ``limit`` bounded queries), 

1624 so nothing unbounded crosses the wire either. Detecting "keys with more 

1625 than one primary" inherently groups the whole collection, so the group 

1626 set itself still scales with the number of distinct source keys (as it 

1627 does on PostgreSQL) — ``allowDiskUse`` covers that. 

1628 """ 

1629 if limit <= 0: 

1630 raise ValueError(f"page limit must be positive, got {limit}") 

1631 if position is CURSOR_END: 

1632 return SourceConflictPage(conflicts=(), next_position=CURSOR_END) 

1633 

1634 match: dict[str, Any] = { 

1635 "file_path": { 

1636 "$type": "string", 

1637 "$nin": ["", "unknown_source", "no-file-path"], 

1638 }, 

1639 "metadata.is_duplicate": {"$ne": True}, 

1640 } 

1641 if isinstance(position, CursorAfter): 

1642 match["file_path"]["$gt"] = self._decode_conflict_cursor(position.opaque) 

1643 

1644 pipeline = [ 

1645 {"$match": match}, 

1646 {"$group": {"_id": "$file_path", "candidate_count": {"$sum": 1}}}, 

1647 {"$match": {"candidate_count": {"$gte": 2}}}, 

1648 {"$sort": {"_id": 1}}, 

1649 {"$limit": limit}, 

1650 ] 

1651 cursor = await self._data.aggregate(pipeline, allowDiskUse=True) 

1652 groups = await cursor.to_list(length=limit) 

1653 

1654 summaries: list[SourceConflictSummary] = [] 

1655 for group in groups: 

1656 canonical = str(group["_id"]) 

1657 summaries.append( 

1658 SourceConflictSummary( 

1659 canonical_source_key=canonical, 

1660 candidate_count=int(group["candidate_count"]), 

1661 sample_doc_ids=await self._primary_candidate_sample(canonical), 

1662 ) 

1663 ) 

1664 conflicts = tuple(summaries) 

1665 if len(groups) < limit: 

1666 next_position: CursorPosition = CURSOR_END 

1667 else: 

1668 next_position = CursorAfter( 

1669 json.dumps(str(groups[-1]["_id"]), ensure_ascii=False) 

1670 ) 

1671 return SourceConflictPage(conflicts=conflicts, next_position=next_position)

1673 async def repair_source_conflict( 

1674 self, 

1675 canonical_source_key: str, 

1676 *, 

1677 primary_doc_id: str, 

1678 expected_candidate_count: int, 

1679 expected_candidate_fingerprint: str, 

1680 dry_run: bool = True, 

1681 ) -> SourceConflictRepairResult: 

1682 """Demote all-but-one primary to duplicate, CAS-guarded (see base). 

1683 

1684 A dry run reads the current candidate set and returns the 

1685 count/fingerprint the operator must echo back. A commit re-reads the 

1686 candidates INSIDE a Mongo transaction; if the count/fingerprint no 

1687 longer match the echoed expectation it raises 

1688 ``SourceConflictRepairCASError`` (CAS — never overwrites a concurrent 

1689 change) and the transaction aborts. Otherwise every losing candidate 

1690 is marked ``metadata.is_duplicate=true`` + 

1691 ``original_doc_id=primary_doc_id`` in the same transaction (content is 

1692 never deleted). ``primary_doc_id`` absent from the current candidate 

1693 set raises ``ValueError``. 

1694 

1695 The transaction gives snapshot isolation, not predicate locking: a new 

1696 primary INSERTed for the same canonical key mid-repair is a phantom the 

1697 snapshot never sees and no write conflict reports. See the base contract 

1698 for what ``committed`` does and does not claim, and for the caller-side 

1699 keyed lock that serializes repair against enqueue. 

1700 """ 

1701 if dry_run: 

1702 candidates = await self._primary_candidates(canonical_source_key) 

1703 count = len(candidates) 

1704 fingerprint = self._conflict_fingerprint(candidates) 

1705 if primary_doc_id not in candidates:

1707 f"primary_doc_id {primary_doc_id!r} is not a current primary " 

1708 f"candidate for {canonical_source_key!r}" 

1709 ) 

1710 demoted = [d for d in candidates if d != primary_doc_id]

1712 canonical_source_key=canonical_source_key, 

1713 primary_doc_id=primary_doc_id, 

1714 candidate_count=count, 

1715 fingerprint=fingerprint, 

1716 demoted_sample_doc_ids=tuple(demoted[: self._CONFLICT_SAMPLE_CAP]),

1718 )

1720 async with self.db.client.start_session() as session: 

1721 async with await session.start_transaction(): 

1722 candidates = await self._primary_candidates( 

1723 canonical_source_key, session=session 

1724 ) 

1725 count = len(candidates)

1814

1854 async def create_edge_indexes_and_migrate_if_not_exists(self) -> None: 

1855 """Create the compound unique edge-endpoint index, migrating legacy edges first. 

1856 

1857 Also ensures the ``source_node_id``/``target_node_id`` single-field 

1858 indexes that back ``node_degree``/``node_degrees_batch``/ 

1859 ``get_node_edges``/``get_nodes_edges_batch`` exist, independently of 

1860 the migration below and on every call (idempotent) — so an 

1861 already-migrated deployment still picks them up. Best-effort: unlike 

1862 the migration, a failure there is logged and does not abort startup. 

1863 

1864 Fail-fast one-time migration (mirrors the OpenSearch canonical-id work): 

1865 

1866 1. dedupe legacy reciprocal duplicate docs, **merging the full relation 

1867 payload** into the survivor (provenance unioned, keywords 

1868 set-unioned, descriptions joined, weight summed — like 

1869 ``_merge_edges_then_upsert``) so no relation evidence is lost; 

1870 2. backfill the canonical ``edge_lo`` / ``edge_hi`` endpoints on every 

1871 remaining doc; 

1872 3. build the partial **compound** unique index on ``(edge_lo, edge_hi)``. 

1873 

1874 The endpoints are two separate fields (not a delimiter-joined string), so 

1875 distinct pairs never collide even if an id contains the would-be 

1876 delimiter — no input sanitisation required. 

1877 

1878 The index doubles as the completion flag: if it already exists we skip. 

1879 Anything failing raises, so ``initialize``/startup aborts rather than 

1880 serving a half-migrated collection (the upsert filter relies on every doc 

1881 having ``edge_lo``/``edge_hi``). Runs inside ``get_data_init_lock``, so 

1882 only the first worker of a deployment migrates; the rest skip on the index. 

1883 

1884 Assumes no concurrent *old-version* writer adds endpoint-less docs after 

1885 this completes (true for stop-the-world / single-deployment restarts). A 

1886 true rolling deploy with mixed code versions writing one collection could 

1887 leave a straggler duplicate; the remedy is to drop the 

1888 ``edge_endpoints_unique`` index and let the next startup re-migrate. 

1889 """ 

1890 workspace_prefix = f"{self.workspace}_" if self.workspace != "" else "" 

1891 index_name = f"{workspace_prefix}edge_endpoints_unique" 

1892 

1893 indexes_cursor = await self.edge_collection.list_indexes() 

1894 existing_indexes = await indexes_cursor.to_list(length=None) 

1895 existing_index_names = {idx.get("name", "") for idx in existing_indexes} 

1896 # Fields already covered by a single-field index. Index options are not 

1897 # inspected: a hand-added collation or partial index the planner can't 

1898 # use for these lookups would still skip creation below. 

1899 single_field_indexed = { 

1900 next(iter(idx["key"])) 

1901 for idx in existing_indexes 

1902 if isinstance(idx.get("key"), dict) and len(idx["key"]) == 1 

1903 } 

1904 

1905 # Best-effort only -- these two indexes are a performance optimization, 

1906 # not required for correctness (unlike the compound migration below). 

1907 # Check by field, not by our own name: an index on the same field can 

1908 # already exist under a different name (e.g. Mongo's own default 

1909 # "source_node_id_1", from a DBA-added index), and creating a 

1910 # same-field index under a new name raises IndexKeySpecsConflict. 

1911 # Catch PyMongoError too (e.g. a restricted service account without 

1912 # createIndex privilege) so a failure here logs and moves on instead 

1913 # of aborting initialize()/startup, mirroring the doc-status index 

1914 # creation above. 

1915 source_index_name = f"{workspace_prefix}source_node_id" 

1916 target_index_name = f"{workspace_prefix}target_node_id" 

1917 if ( 

1918 "source_node_id" not in single_field_indexed 

1919 or "target_node_id" not in single_field_indexed 

1920 ): 

1921 # create_index() awaits the build's commit, and this runs inside 

1922 # get_data_init_lock, so the first startup after upgrading onto 

1923 # this code blocks here until the build finishes -- on a 

1924 # collection with tens of millions of edges that can look like a 

1925 # hang rather than a one-time index build. Logged unconditionally 

1926 # (not just on a slow-build heuristic) since there's no cheap way 

1927 # to know the collection size in advance. 

1928 logger.info( 

1929 f"[{self.workspace}] Creating source_node_id/target_node_id " 

1930 f"indexes on {self._edge_collection_name}; this may take a " 

1931 "while on large collections and blocks startup until it " 

1932 "completes" 

1933 ) 

1934 if "source_node_id" not in single_field_indexed: 

1935 try: 

1936 await self.edge_collection.create_index( 

1937 [("source_node_id", 1)], name=source_index_name 

1938 ) 

1939 except PyMongoError as e: 

1940 logger.warning( 

1941 f"[{self.workspace}] Could not create source_node_id index on " 

1942 f"{self._edge_collection_name}: {e}. Queries filtering by " 

1943 "source_node_id will fall back to a collection scan." 

1944 ) 

1945 if "target_node_id" not in single_field_indexed: 

1946 try: 

1947 await self.edge_collection.create_index( 

1948 [("target_node_id", 1)], name=target_index_name 

1949 ) 

1950 except PyMongoError as e: 

1951 logger.warning( 

1952 f"[{self.workspace}] Could not create target_node_id index on " 

1953 f"{self._edge_collection_name}: {e}. Queries filtering by " 

1954 "target_node_id will fall back to a collection scan." 

1955 ) 

1956 

1957 if index_name in existing_index_names: 

1958 logger.info( 

1959 f"[{self.workspace}] Edge collection {self._edge_collection_name} " 

1960 f"already on canonical edge endpoints; skipping migration" 

1961 ) 

1962 return 

1963 

1964 # Best-effort total for an X/total denominator (estimated_document_count 

1965 # is O(1) metadata); migration still works if it is unavailable. 

1966 try: 

1967 total = await self.edge_collection.estimated_document_count() 

1968 except PyMongoError: 

1969 total = None 

1970 logger.info( 

1971 f"[{self.workspace}] Starting canonical edge migration for " 

1972 f"{self._edge_collection_name}" 

1973 + (f" (~{total} edges to scan)" if total is not None else "") 

1974 ) 

1975 

1976 removed = await self._dedupe_legacy_edges() 

1977 backfilled = await self._backfill_edge_endpoints() 

1978 # The unique index is the completion flag — only created on full success. 

1979 # unique build raises if any duplicate slipped through (e.g. a concurrent 

1980 # old-version writer), which fails startup so the next run retries. 

1981 await self.edge_collection.create_index( 

1982 [("edge_lo", 1), ("edge_hi", 1)], 

1983 name=index_name, 

1984 unique=True, 

1985 partialFilterExpression={ 

1986 "edge_lo": {"$exists": True, "$type": "string"}, 

1987 "edge_hi": {"$exists": True, "$type": "string"}, 

1988 }, 

1989 ) 

1990 scanned = total if total is not None else "?" 

1991 logger.info( 

1992 f"[{self.workspace}] Canonical edge migration complete for " 

1993 f"{self._edge_collection_name}: scanned {scanned}, deduped {removed}, " 

1994 f"backfilled {backfilled}" 

1995 ) 

1996 

1997 async def _dedupe_legacy_edges(self) -> int: 

1998 """Collapse duplicate docs for the same undirected edge into one. 

1999 

2000 Groups by the canonical (sorted) endpoint pair; for each group with more 

2001 than one doc, keeps the newest by ``created_at`` and **merges the 

2002 non-survivors' relation payload into it before deleting them** so no 

2003 relation evidence is lost: ``source_ids``/``source_id``/``file_path`` and 

2004 ``description`` are unioned over their ``GRAPH_FIELD_SEP`` components, 

2005 ``keywords`` are comma-set-unioned, and ``weight`` is **summed** (like 

2006 ``_merge_edges_then_upsert`` — duplicate docs carry separate accumulated 

2007 weight) then floored to the merged evidence count, so a duplicate with 

2008 new source_ids but a missing/non-numeric legacy weight cannot leave the 

2009 result under its own evidence count. 

2010 

2011 The merge is **idempotent across retries**: if a transient error aborts 

2012 startup after the survivor update but before the delete, the next run 

2013 re-processes the same group and must produce the same survivor. The union 

2014 fields union their split components (re-merging an already-merged 

2015 survivor is a no-op), and the weight sum counts the survivor's current 

2016 weight once plus each other duplicate only while its source_ids are not 

2017 yet folded into the survivor — so a retry (whose survivor already 

2018 contains them) does not double-count. Returns the number of docs removed. 

2019 """ 

2020 pipeline = [ 

2021 { 

2022 "$group": { 

2023 "_id": { 

2024 "lo": { 

2025 "$cond": [ 

2026 {"$lte": ["$source_node_id", "$target_node_id"]}, 

2027 "$source_node_id", 

2028 "$target_node_id", 

2029 ] 

2030 }, 

2031 "hi": { 

2032 "$cond": [ 

2033 {"$lte": ["$source_node_id", "$target_node_id"]}, 

2034 "$target_node_id", 

2035 "$source_node_id", 

2036 ] 

2037 }, 

2038 }, 

2039 "docs": { 

2040 "$push": { 

2041 "_id": "$_id", 

2042 "source_id": "$source_id", 

2043 "source_ids": "$source_ids", 

2044 "file_path": "$file_path", 

2045 "description": "$description", 

2046 "keywords": "$keywords", 

2047 "weight": "$weight", 

2048 "created_at": "$created_at", 

2049 } 

2050 }, 

2051 "count": {"$sum": 1}, 

2052 } 

2053 }, 

2054 {"$match": {"count": {"$gt": 1}}}, 

2055 ] 

2056 removed = 0 

2057 next_progress = _EDGE_MIGRATION_PROGRESS_INTERVAL 

2058 cursor = await self.edge_collection.aggregate(pipeline, allowDiskUse=True) 

2059 async for group in cursor: 

2060 docs = group["docs"] 

2061 survivor = max(docs, key=lambda d: d.get("created_at") or 0) 

2062 others = [d for d in docs if d["_id"] != survivor["_id"]] 

2063 if not others: 2063 ↛ 2064line 2063 didn't jump to line 2064 because the condition on line 2063 was never true

2064 continue 

2065 

2066 # Merge the full relation payload across ALL docs (survivor included). 

2067 # The union fields (source_ids/file_path/description/keywords) union 

2068 # their split components, so re-merging an already-merged survivor (a 

2069 # fail-fast retry) is a no-op. 

2070 all_source_ids: list[str] = [] 

2071 all_file_paths: list[str] = [] 

2072 all_descriptions: list[str] = [] 

2073 all_keywords: set[str] = set() 

2074 for d in docs: 

2075 all_source_ids = merge_source_ids( 

2076 all_source_ids, _edge_source_id_list(d) 

2077 ) 

2078 fp = d.get("file_path") 

2079 all_file_paths = merge_source_ids( 

2080 all_file_paths, fp.split(GRAPH_FIELD_SEP) if fp else [] 

2081 ) 

2082 desc = d.get("description") 

2083 all_descriptions = merge_source_ids( 

2084 all_descriptions, desc.split(GRAPH_FIELD_SEP) if desc else [] 

2085 ) 

2086 kw = d.get("keywords") 

2087 if kw: 

2088 all_keywords.update(k.strip() for k in kw.split(",") if k.strip()) 

2089 

2090 # Weight is summed like _merge_edges_then_upsert (duplicate docs carry 

2091 # separate accumulated evidence), but idempotently: the survivor's 

2092 # current weight is the base (counted once) and each other duplicate 

2093 # adds its weight ONLY if its source_ids are not already folded into 

2094 # the survivor. On a fail-fast retry the survivor already contains the 

2095 # others' source_ids, so they are skipped and the sum stays stable. 

2096 # Legacy string weights are coerced; non-numeric values are skipped so 

2097 # the migration cannot crash on a bad value. 

2098 survivor_sids = set(_edge_source_id_list(survivor)) 

2099 weights: list[float] = [] 

2100 sw = _coerce_weight(survivor.get("weight")) 

2101 if sw is not None: 

2102 weights.append(sw) 

2103 for o in others: 

2104 o_sids = set(_edge_source_id_list(o)) 

2105 if not o_sids or o_sids <= survivor_sids: 

2106 continue # no new trackable evidence -> don't (re-)add weight 

2107 ow = _coerce_weight(o.get("weight")) 

2108 if ow is not None: 

2109 weights.append(ow) 

2110 

2111 set_fields: dict[str, Any] = {} 

2112 if all_source_ids: 2112 ↛ 2115line 2112 didn't jump to line 2115 because the condition on line 2112 was always true

2113 set_fields["source_ids"] = all_source_ids 

2114 set_fields["source_id"] = GRAPH_FIELD_SEP.join(all_source_ids) 

2115 if all_file_paths: 

2116 set_fields["file_path"] = GRAPH_FIELD_SEP.join(all_file_paths) 

2117 if all_descriptions: 

2118 set_fields["description"] = GRAPH_FIELD_SEP.join(all_descriptions) 

2119 if all_keywords: 

2120 set_fields["keywords"] = ",".join(sorted(all_keywords)) 

2121 # A duplicate can contribute new source_ids while carrying a 

2122 # missing/non-numeric weight (skipped above), which would otherwise 

2123 # let the summed weight fall below the merged evidence count -- or, 

2124 # if every doc lacked a coercible weight, leave "weight" unset even 

2125 # though source_ids just grew. Floor the sum to the evidence count, 

2126 # per the relation weight contract, whichever a plain sum misses. 

2127 # 

2128 # The floor is computed from `relation_evidence_count` rather than 

2129 # through `apply_relation_weight_floor`, which validates the whole 

2130 # relation the way a caller ingress does: a legacy `source_id` no 

2131 # backend can store (an XML-incompatible character, say) would abort 

2132 # this one-time migration over a row it is supposed to carry 

2133 # through. Counting evidence needs no such validation. 

2134 evidence_count = relation_evidence_count(set_fields.get("source_id", "")) 

2135 if weights or evidence_count: 

2136 summed_weight = sum(weights) if weights else 0.0 

2137 if summed_weight == math.inf: 

2138 # Each weight was individually finite (_coerce_weight 

2139 # rejects nan/inf inputs), but their sum can still overflow 

2140 # past what a graph attribute may hold. Keep the largest 

2141 # representable weight instead of collapsing an absurd but 

2142 # real magnitude down to the evidence count. Only +inf is 

2143 # clamped: a sum of finite floats is never NaN, and -inf is 

2144 # absorbed by the evidence floor below. 

2145 summed_weight = sys.float_info.max 

2146 set_fields["weight"] = max(summed_weight, float(evidence_count)) 

2147 if set_fields: 2147 ↛ 2151line 2147 didn't jump to line 2151 because the condition on line 2147 was always true

2148 await self.edge_collection.update_one( 

2149 {"_id": survivor["_id"]}, {"$set": set_fields} 

2150 ) 

2151 await self.edge_collection.delete_many( 

2152 {"_id": {"$in": [d["_id"] for d in others]}} 

2153 ) 

2154 removed += len(others) 

2155 if removed >= next_progress: 2155 ↛ 2156line 2155 didn't jump to line 2156 because the condition on line 2155 was never true

2156 logger.info( 

2157 f"[{self.workspace}] Canonical edge migration progress: " 

2158 f"deduped {removed} duplicate doc(s) so far" 

2159 ) 

2160 next_progress += _EDGE_MIGRATION_PROGRESS_INTERVAL 

2161 return removed

2163 async def _backfill_edge_endpoints(self) -> int: 

2164 """Set the canonical ``edge_lo``/``edge_hi`` on every doc that lacks them. 

2165 

2166 Returns the modified count. Runs after dedupe, so each canonical pair has 

2167 one doc and the backfilled (edge_lo, edge_hi) pairs are unique. 

2168 """ 

2169 is_sorted = {"$lte": ["$source_node_id", "$target_node_id"]} 

2170 result = await self.edge_collection.update_many( 

2171 {"edge_lo": {"$exists": False}}, 

2172 [ 

2173 { 

2174 "$set": { 

2175 "edge_lo": { 

2176 "$cond": [ 

2177 is_sorted, 

2178 "$source_node_id", 

2179 "$target_node_id", 

2180 ] 

2181 }, 

2182 "edge_hi": { 

2183 "$cond": [ 

2184 is_sorted, 

2185 "$target_node_id", 

2186 "$source_node_id", 

2187 ] 

2188 }, 

2189 } 

2190 } 

2191 ], 

2192 ) 

2193 return result.modified_count

2238 async def has_edge(self, source_node_id: str, target_node_id: str) -> bool: 

2239 """ 

2240 Check if there's a direct single-hop edge between source_node_id and target_node_id. 

2241 

2242 Matches on the canonical ``(edge_lo, edge_hi)`` pair (direction-independent) 

2243 instead of the bidirectional ``$or``, so this point lookup is served by the

2247 edge_lo, edge_hi = _canonical_edge_endpoints(source_node_id, target_node_id) 

2248 doc = await self.edge_collection.find_one( 

2249 {"edge_lo": edge_lo, "edge_hi": edge_hi}, 

2250 {"_id": 1}, 

2251 ) 

2252 return doc is not None

2260 async def node_degree(self, node_id: str) -> int: 

2261 """ 

2262 Returns the total number of edges connected to node_id (both inbound and outbound).

2802 async def upsert_edges_batch( 

2803 self, edges: list[tuple[str, str, dict[str, str]]] 

2804 ) -> None: 

2805 """Batch insert/update multiple edges using a single bulk_write() call. 

2806 

2807 Also ensures BOTH endpoints of every edge exist (matching upsert_edge() 

2808 behaviour) via a separate bulk_write on the node collection for any 

2809 endpoint that needs to be created as an empty placeholder. 

2810 

2811 Args: 

2812 edges: List of (source_node_id, target_node_id, edge_data) tuples. 

2813 """ 

2814 if not edges: 2814 ↛ 2815line 2814 didn't jump to line 2815 because the condition on line 2814 was never true

2815 return 

2816 

2817 # Whole batch first: the endpoint-placeholder bulk_write below happens 

2818 # before any edge document is written, so rejecting mid-loop would leave 

2819 # placeholder nodes behind for edges that were never created. 

2820 # 

2821 # Snapshot each mapping as it is validated and use the snapshots for the 

2822 # documents built after the placeholder await -- see upsert_edge for the 

2823 # window that closes. 

2824 validated_edges: list[tuple[str, str, dict]] = [] 

2825 for src, tgt, edge_data in edges: 

2826 edge_attributes = dict(edge_data) 

2827 self._validate_attribute_names( 

2828 edge_attributes, context=self._edge_context(src, tgt) 

2829 ) 

2830 validated_edges.append((src, tgt, edge_attributes)) 

2831 

2832 # Both endpoints, not just the source — see upsert_edge for why a 

2833 # target-only endpoint is externally visible as an inconsistency. 

2834 endpoint_ids = list( 

2835 dict.fromkeys( 

2836 node_id for src, tgt, _data in edges for node_id in (src, tgt) 

2837 ) 

2838 ) 

2839 node_ops: list[tuple[Any, int, str]] = [ 

2840 ( 

2841 UpdateOne({"_id": nid}, {"$setOnInsert": {"_id": nid}}, upsert=True), 

2842 _estimate_doc_bytes({"_id": nid}), 

2843 nid, 

2844 ) 

2845 for nid in endpoint_ids 

2846 ] 

2847 await _run_batched_bulk_write( 

2848 self.collection, 

2849 node_ops, 

2850 max_payload_bytes=self._max_upsert_payload_bytes, 

2851 max_records_per_batch=self._max_upsert_records_per_batch, 

2852 ordered=False, 

2853 log_prefix=f"[{self.workspace}] {self.namespace} edges:", 

2854 what="edge endpoint placeholder upsert", 

2855 ) 

2856 

2857 # Key every edge by its canonical (edge_lo, edge_hi) pair and dedupe 

2858 # within the batch (last-write-wins). Deduping collapses reciprocal 

2859 # directions onto one op, which both matches the compound unique index 

2860 # and avoids an intra-batch duplicate-key error from two ops inserting 

2861 # the same endpoint pair. 

2862 deduped_ops: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[Any, int, str]] = {} 

2863 for source_node_id, target_node_id, edge_attributes in validated_edges: 

2864 update_doc: dict = {"$set": dict(edge_attributes)} 

2865 if edge_attributes.get("source_id", ""): 

2866 update_doc["$set"]["source_ids"] = edge_attributes["source_id"].split( 

2867 GRAPH_FIELD_SEP 

2868 ) 

2869 update_doc["$set"]["source_node_id"] = source_node_id 

2870 update_doc["$set"]["target_node_id"] = target_node_id 

2871 edge_lo, edge_hi = _canonical_edge_endpoints(source_node_id, target_node_id) 

2872 update_doc["$set"]["edge_lo"] = edge_lo 

2873 update_doc["$set"]["edge_hi"] = edge_hi 

2874 deduped_ops[(edge_lo, edge_hi)] = ( 

2875 UpdateOne( 

2876 {"edge_lo": edge_lo, "edge_hi": edge_hi}, update_doc, upsert=True 

2877 ), 

2878 _estimate_doc_bytes(update_doc), 

2879 f"{source_node_id}->{target_node_id}", 

2880 ) 

2881 edge_ops = list(deduped_ops.values()) 

2882 

2883 # ordered=True (kept from the pre-canonical behaviour). Intra-batch 

2884 # last-write-wins is already guaranteed by the endpoint-pair dedupe above 

2885 # (one op per pair), so ordering is not load-bearing for that; we keep it 

2886 # for continuity. If a concurrent writer (another process bypassing the keyed 

2887 # lock) wins an insert, our upsert hits 11000 and the bulk aborts; we 

2888 # retry the whole op list once — the racing docs now exist, so the 

2889 # upserts update instead of inserting (idempotent). A non-11000 / write- 

2890 # concern error re-raises rather than being masked. 

2891 async def _run_edge_bulk() -> None: 

2892 await _run_batched_bulk_write( 

2893 self.edge_collection, 

2894 edge_ops, 

2895 max_payload_bytes=self._max_upsert_payload_bytes, 

2896 max_records_per_batch=self._max_upsert_records_per_batch, 

2897 ordered=True, 

2898 log_prefix=f"[{self.workspace}] {self.namespace} edges:", 

2899 what="edge upsert", 

2900 ) 

2901 

2902 try: 

2903 await _run_edge_bulk() 

2904 except BulkWriteError as e: 

2905 details = e.details or {} 

2906 write_errors = details.get("writeErrors", []) 

2907 # Retry ONLY when every failure is a duplicate-key race; a 

2908 # writeConcern failure (durability problem, empty writeErrors) or any 

2909 # other write error must surface, not be masked by a blind retry. 

2910 # 

2911 # NOTE: under ordered=True the bulk aborts at the FIRST failing op, so 

2912 # writeErrors holds at most one entry — the all(...) check therefore 

2913 # only inspects that first error, not the whole batch. Ops after it 

2914 # never ran; they re-run when we retry the entire op list below. So a 

2915 # non-11000 error hidden behind a leading 11000 is not masked — it 

2916 # simply surfaces one retry later (the retry hits it and re-raises, 

2917 # since by then the leading dup has resolved to a plain update). 

2918 dup_only = ( 

2919 bool(write_errors) 

2920 and all(we.get("code") == _DUPLICATE_KEY_CODE for we in write_errors) 

2921 and not details.get("writeConcernErrors") 

2922 ) 

2923 if not dup_only: 

2924 raise 

2925 logger.debug( 

2926 f"[{self.workspace}] {self.namespace} edges: {len(write_errors)} " 

2927 f"duplicate-key race(s) on edge upsert; retrying as updates" 

2928 ) 

2929 await _run_edge_bulk()

3039 async def _rank_edge_endpoints_by_degree( 

3040 self, limit: int, skip: int = 0 

3041 ) -> list[str]: 

3042 """Rank edge endpoints by undirected degree, ties on the label ascending. 

3043 

3044 Paged rather than fetched whole because the ``$limit`` runs server-side: 

3045 the caller cannot tell how many of a page really have node documents 

3046 until it has fetched them, so it needs a way to ask for the next ones. 

3047 The sort is a TOTAL order -- degree descending, then the unique ``_id`` 

3048 -- which is what makes ``$skip`` paging over it stable across passes. 

3049 """ 

3050 if limit <= 0: 3050 ↛ 3051line 3050 didn't jump to line 3051 because the condition on line 3050 was never true

3051 return [] 

3052 

3053 pipeline: list[dict[str, Any]] = [ 

3054 {"$project": {"source_node_id": 1, "_id": 0}}, 

3055 {"$group": {"_id": "$source_node_id", "degree": {"$sum": 1}}}, 

3056 { 

3057 "$unionWith": { 

3058 "coll": self._edge_collection_name, 

3059 "pipeline": [ 

3060 {"$project": {"target_node_id": 1, "_id": 0}}, 

3061 { 

3062 "$group": { 

3063 "_id": "$target_node_id", 

3064 "degree": {"$sum": 1}, 

3065 } 

3066 }, 

3067 ], 

3068 } 

3069 }, 

3070 {"$group": {"_id": "$_id", "degree": {"$sum": "$degree"}}}, 

3071 # Degree descending, then label ascending. The tie-break is the 

3072 # BaseGraphStorage contract: $limit cuts a band of equal-degree 

3073 # entities, and without a second sort key which ones survive is 

3074 # whatever order the aggregation happens to emit. 

3075 {"$sort": {"degree": -1, "_id": 1}}, 

3076 ] 

3077 if skip: 

3078 pipeline.append({"$skip": skip}) 

3079 pipeline.append({"$limit": limit}) 

3080 

3081 cursor = await self.edge_collection.aggregate(pipeline, allowDiskUse=True) 

3082 return [str(doc["_id"]) async for doc in cursor]

3084 async def _accept_existing_nodes( 

3085 self, 

3086 candidate_ids: list[str], 

3087 limit: int, 

3088 result: KnowledgeGraph, 

3089 accepted: list[str], 

3090 ) -> None: 

3091 """Append the candidates that really have node documents, up to `limit`. 

3092 

3093 ``_fetch_nodes_by_ids`` preserves the requested order and drops ids with 

3094 no document, so consuming it in order preserves the ranking and never 

3095 lets an id that resolves to nothing occupy a slot. 

3096 

3097 Asks for the current shortfall first and for the remainder only if that 

3098 did not fill it, so at most two queries: the caller passes whole ranked 

3099 pages, and filling the handful of slots a few dangling ids vacated must 

3100 not pull a page of node documents to place a few nodes. 

3101 """ 

3102 if not candidate_ids or len(accepted) >= limit: 3102 ↛ 3103line 3102 didn't jump to line 3103 because the condition on line 3102 was never true

3103 return 

3104 

3105 head = candidate_ids[: limit - len(accepted)] 

3106 for chunk in (head, candidate_ids[len(head) :]): 

3107 if not chunk or len(accepted) >= limit: 

3108 break 

3109 docs = await self._fetch_nodes_by_ids(chunk, {"source_ids": 0}) 

3110 for doc in docs: 

3111 if len(accepted) >= limit: 3111 ↛ 3112line 3111 didn't jump to line 3112 because the condition on line 3111 was never true

3112 break 

3113 accepted.append(str(doc["_id"])) 

3114 result.nodes.append(self._construct_graph_node(doc["_id"], doc))

3118 ) -> KnowledgeGraph: 

3119 """ 

3120 It's possible that the node with one or multiple relationships is retrieved, 

3121 while its neighbor is not. Then this node might seem like disconnected in UI. 

3122 """ 

3123 

3124 total_node_count = await self.collection.count_documents({}) 

3125 result = KnowledgeGraph() 

3126 seen_edges = set() 

3127 

3128 result.is_truncated = total_node_count > max_nodes 

3129 if result.is_truncated: 3129 ↛ 3199line 3129 didn't jump to line 3199 because the condition on line 3129 was always true

3130 # The ranked ids are edge ENDPOINTS, and upsert_edge only guarantees 

3131 # the source node exists, so one can be a dangling id with no node 

3132 # document -- a legacy state this backend deliberately tolerates 

3133 # (see the traversal, which counts only documents it actually read). 

3134 # Taking the $limit as final let such an id consume a slot and the 

3135 # answer came back short, reachable as soon as ties break on the 

3136 # label because a dangling label sorts like any other. 

3137 # Page the band until the cap fills or the band runs out, so a 

3138 # vacated slot always goes to the next-ranked entry. The loop is 

3139 # what keeps the top-up below meaning what it says: it is reachable 

3140 # only once every edge-backed entity has been offered a slot, so 

3141 # everything it can still pick really is degree-0. Stopping earlier 

3142 # would let an isolate outrank an entity further down the band -- 

3143 # only ONE dangling id in this page plus one in the next is enough 

3144 # to reach that, so it is not a corner. 

3145 # 

3146 # Whole pages, not shortfall-sized ones: a page is {_id, degree} 

3147 # rows, cheap next to the aggregation that produces it, so each 

3148 # extra pass should make as much progress as it can. The document 

3149 # fetch inside _accept_existing_nodes stays shortfall-sized. 

3150 node_ids: list[str] = [] 

3151 skip = 0

3153 ranked_page = await self._rank_edge_endpoints_by_degree( 

3154 max_nodes, skip=skip 

3155 ) 

3156 skip += len(ranked_page)

3158 ranked_page, max_nodes, result, node_ids 

3159 )

3161 break # short page: the band is exhausted 

3162

3174 self.collection.find( 

3175 {"_id": {"$nin": list(node_ids)}}, 

3176 {"source_ids": 0},

3194 ] 

3195 } 

3196 )

3199 cursor = self.collection.find({}, {"source_ids": 0}) 

3200

3202 result.nodes.append(self._construct_graph_node(doc["_id"], doc)) 

3203 

3204 edge_cursor = self.edge_collection.find({})

3214 async def _bidirectional_bfs_nodes( 

3215 self,

3217 seen_nodes: set[str],

3227 # the cap can discard any of it (the pre-ranking loop could stop at the

3271 { 

3272 "$or": [ 

3273 {"source_node_id": {"$in": node_labels}}, 

3274 {"target_node_id": {"$in": node_labels}}, 

3275 ] 

3276 } 

3277 )

3289 )

3669 async def get_popular_labels(self, limit: int = 300) -> list[str]:

3699 "$unionWith": { 

3700 "coll": self._edge_collection_name, 

3701 "pipeline": [ 

3702 { 

3703 "$group": { 

3704 "_id": "$target_node_id", 

3705 "in_degree": {"$sum": 1}, 

3706 } 

3707 }

3709 } 

3710 },

3713 "$group": { 

3714 "_id": "$_id", 

3715 "total_degree": { 

3716 "$sum": { 

3717 "$add": [ 

3718 {"$ifNull": ["$out_degree", 0]}, 

3719 {"$ifNull": ["$in_degree", 0]}, 

3720 ] 

3721 } 

3722 }, 

3723 } 

3724 }, 

3725 # Sort by degree descending, then by label ascending 

3726 {"$sort": {"total_degree": -1, "_id": 1}},

3728 {"$limit": limit}, 

3729 # Project only the label

4138 

4139# The embedding-space marker lives in the vector collection's JSON Schema 

4140# validator ``description``, never in a document. A marker document would be a 

4141# row in the data collection that every future full-collection scan owes an 

4142# exclusion; the validator is metadata and owes nothing, and no read path -- 

4143# ``$vectorSearch`` or the ``_id`` / ``src_id`` / ``tgt_id`` finds -- can reach 

4144# it. See ``docs/design/VectorSpaceProvenance.md``. 

4145# 

4146# The prefix is what makes a foreign description unambiguously "not ours" 

4147# rather than something to be parsed and possibly misread, and it makes the 

4148# marker legible to an operator running ``db.getCollectionInfos()``. 

4149_VECTOR_SPACE_DESCRIPTION_PREFIX = "LightRAG embedding space: " 

4150 

4151 

4152def _vector_space_validator(embedding_func, existing: Any = None) -> dict: 

4153 """``existing`` with this instance's embedding space recorded in it. 

4154 

4155 MERGED, never replaced. ``collMod`` takes the whole validator, so writing a 

4156 bare marker schema would drop every rule an operator put on the collection 

4157 -- their ``required`` list, their ``properties`` -- from all future writes, 

4158 silently, on an ordinary ``/documents/clear``. That is the same hazard 

4159 OpenSearch's ``put_mapping`` has with ``_meta``, and it is answered the same 

4160 way: read what is there and add to it. 

4161 

4162 Only ``$jsonSchema.description`` is taken over, because that is the field 

4163 the marker lives in. An operator who used it for prose loses that prose; 

4164 that is the documented cost of this marker home, and it is a far smaller 

4165 one than losing validation rules. A validator with no ``$jsonSchema`` (a 

4166 plain query expression) keeps its operators: a validator is an implicit 

4167 AND, so the added ``$jsonSchema`` sits beside them, and ``bsonType: 

4168 object`` matches every document, so it rejects nothing on its own. 

4169 """ 

4170 payload = json.dumps(vector_space_marker(embedding_func), sort_keys=True) 

4171 merged = dict(existing) if isinstance(existing, dict) else {} 

4172 schema = merged.get("$jsonSchema") 

4173 schema = dict(schema) if isinstance(schema, dict) else {} 

4174 schema.setdefault("bsonType", "object") 

4175 schema["description"] = _VECTOR_SPACE_DESCRIPTION_PREFIX + payload 

4176 merged["$jsonSchema"] = schema 

4177 return merged 

4178 

4179 

4180def _read_validator_vector_space(validator: Any) -> tuple[str | None, int | None]: 

4181 """Extract ``(model, dim)`` from a stored validator, or ``(None, None)``. 

4182 

4183 Every way this can fail reads as "not recorded": no validator, a validator 

4184 written by something other than LightRAG, a truncated or hand-edited 

4185 payload. A marker we cannot read is not evidence of a mismatch. 

4186 """ 

4187 if not isinstance(validator, dict): 

4188 return None, None 

4189 description = (validator.get("$jsonSchema") or {}).get("description") 

4190 if not isinstance(description, str) or not description.startswith( 

4191 _VECTOR_SPACE_DESCRIPTION_PREFIX 

4192 ): 

4193 return None, None 

4194 try: 

4195 payload = json.loads(description[len(_VECTOR_SPACE_DESCRIPTION_PREFIX) :]) 

4196 except ValueError: 

4197 return None, None 

4198 return read_vector_space_marker(payload)

4480 """Create the Atlas Vector Search index, repairing a FAILED one.

4485 ``cannot query vector index ... while in state FAILED``. Matching the 

4486 index only by name would treat that dead index as healthy and wedge 

4487 all queries permanently, so a non-queryable, same-dimension FAILED 

4488 index is dropped and rebuilt here. 

4489 

4490 Two guards run *before* the rebuild: (1) a FAILED index that is still 

4491 ``queryable`` (a background rebuild/update failed but the previously 

4492 built index keeps serving) is left in place to avoid taking a 

4493 still-serving index offline; (2) a FAILED index built for a different 

4494 DIMENSION raises rather than being auto-rebuilt against incompatible 

4495 stored vectors. A same-dimension model change is invisible here --

5110 async def _reprovision_vector_space(self) -> None: 

5111 """Rebuild the emptied collection for THIS instance's embedding space. 

5112 

5113 The step that makes a refusal recoverable on this backend. ``drop()`` 

5114 used to go straight to ``create_vector_index_if_not_exists()``, which 

5115 re-read the SURVIVING Atlas search index definition and raised the same 

5116 dimension mismatch again -- ``delete_many({})`` removes documents, not 

5117 the index, and not the validator either. ``except PyMongoError`` did not 

5118 catch that raise, so the drop failed and the operator was left deleting 

5119 the index out of band. Three things have to happen here, in this order: 

5120 

5121 1. **Drop the search index when its dimension is wrong.** Only then: 

5122 the definition records a dimension and nothing else, so a 

5123 same-dimension MODEL change leaves a perfectly good index, and 

5124 rebuilding it would cost an Atlas index build for nothing. 

5125 2. **Rewrite the validator marker.** The collection is empty, so this 

5126 process's embedding space is now trivially the true one. Skipping it 

5127 would leave the previous model recorded and make the NEXT 

5128 ``initialize()`` refuse again -- the recovery would not converge. 

5129 3. **Recreate the index**, which is now either absent or compatible, so 

5130 the guard inside it cannot fire. 

5131 """ 

5132 index_dim = await self._read_search_index_dimension() 

5133 expected_dim = self.embedding_func.embedding_dim 

5134 if index_dim is not None and index_dim != expected_dim: 

5135 logger.warning( 

5136 f"[{self.workspace}] Dropping vector index {self._index_name}: it was " 

5137 f"built for dimension {index_dim} and this instance embeds at " 

5138 f"{expected_dim}" 

5139 ) 

5140 await self._data.drop_search_index(self._index_name) 

5141 await self._wait_for_search_index_absent(self._index_name) 

5142 if not await self._record_vector_space_marker(): 

5143 # A denied write does not leave the collection unmarked -- it 

5144 # leaves whatever was there. On a collection previously marked for 

5145 # another model that is the PREVIOUS model's name, and the attach 

5146 # that ``clear_vector_space_refusal`` runs straight after this drop 

5147 # is refused all over again. Every vector is already gone by then, 

5148 # so the one thing this must not do is report success: that would 

5149 # send the tool off to rebuild into a collection it cannot attach 

5150 # to. Fail loud instead, naming the permission that is missing. 

5151 # 

5152 # When nothing conflicting is recorded the denial really does 

5153 # reduce to "unmarked", and that is not a failure -- it is where 

5154 # every collection was before this feature existed. 

5155 try: 

5156 await self._assert_collection_is_usable() 

5157 except VectorSpaceMismatchError as e: 

5158 raise StorageControlPlaneError( 

5159 f"[{self.workspace}] Dropped every vector in " 

5160 f"'{self._collection_name}', but could not rewrite its " 

5161 f"embedding-space marker: the collection still records the " 

5162 f"previous model, so the rebuild would be refused. Grant " 

5163 f"collMod on this collection and run lightrag-rebuild-vdb " 

5164 f"again." 

5165 ) from e 

5166 await self.create_vector_index_if_not_exists() 

5167 

5168 async def drop(self) -> dict[str, str]: 

5169 """Drop all documents and re-provision the collection. Destructive. 

5170 

5171 Also the recovery path for an embedding-space refusal: the collection 

5172 comes back empty and marked for THIS instance's model, so the next 

5173 ``initialize()`` attaches normally. See ``_reprovision_vector_space``. 

5174 

5175 MUST only be called when ``pipeline_status`` is idle (see the 

5176 Pipeline concurrency contract in ``docs/design/PipelineConcurrencyContract.md``); the only 

5177 in-tree caller ``clear_documents`` enforces this. 

5178 

5179 Caveat — only this instance's buffers are cleared. Other 

5180 ``MongoVectorDBStorage`` instances aliased onto the same 

5181 ``final_namespace`` (multi-worker processes, or distinct 

5182 workspaces collapsed by ``MONGODB_WORKSPACE``) keep their own 

5183 buffers; a sibling whose prior flush failed and left buffers 

5184 intact will, on its next flush, bulk-write those stale rows into 

5185 the freshly recreated collection. Direct callers bypassing the 

5186 idle precondition MUST flush every aliased instance first. 

5187 

5188 Returns: 

5189 dict[str, str]: ``{"status": "success"|"error", "message": str}`` 

5190 """ 

5191 try: 

5192 async with self._flush_lock: 

5193 # Discard any buffered writes before the collection is wiped; 

5194 # a concurrent flush would otherwise resurrect them. 

5195 self._pending_vector_docs.clear() 

5196 self._pending_vector_deletes.clear() 

5197 

5198 # Delete all documents 

5199 result = await self._data.delete_many({}) 

5200 deleted_count = result.deleted_count 

5201 

5202 # Re-provision in the CURRENT embedding space, not the one the 

5203 # collection used to hold. 

5204 await self._reprovision_vector_space() 

5205 

5206 logger.info( 

5207 f"[{self.workspace}] Dropped {deleted_count} documents from vector storage {self._collection_name} and recreated vector index" 

5208 ) 

5209 return { 

5210 "status": "success", 

5211 "message": f"{deleted_count} documents dropped and vector index recreated", 

5212 } 

5213 except PyMongoError as e: 

5214 logger.error( 

5215 f"[{self.workspace}] Error dropping vector storage {self._collection_name}: {e}" 

5216 ) 

5217 return {"status": "error", "message": str(e)} 

5218 except StorageControlPlaneError as e: 

5219 # Re-provisioning failed after the documents were already deleted. 

5220 # The deletion is real and irreversible; what is NOT true is that 

5221 # the collection is ready to be rebuilt, so this must not be 

5222 # reported as a success. See _reprovision_vector_space. 

5223 logger.error(f"[{self.workspace}] {e}") 

5224 return {"status": "error", "message": str(e)} 

5225

5227async def get_or_create_collection( 

5228 db: AsyncDatabase, collection_name: str, validator: dict | None = None 

5229): 

5230 """Return the collection, creating it with ``validator`` if it is absent. 

5231 

5232 ``validator`` is applied ONLY at creation. An existing collection keeps 

5233 whatever it has: overwriting a validator on attach would stamp this 

5234 process's embedding-space marker onto vectors it did not write. See 

5235 ``docs/design/VectorSpaceProvenance.md``. 

5236 """ 

5237 collection_names = await db.list_collection_names() 

5238 

5239 if collection_name not in collection_names: 

5240 kwargs = {"validator": validator} if validator else {} 

5241 collection = await db.create_collection(collection_name, **kwargs) 

5242 logger.info(f"Created collection: {collection_name}") 

5243 return collection 

5244 else: 

5245 logger.debug(f"Collection '{collection_name}' already exists.") 

5246 return db.get_collection(collection_name)
